theme: Unity; spiritual gifts; the new self
readingInstruction: Read Ephesians 4:1-32. The letter turns from “what God has done” to “how we then should live.” Read the first sixteen verses on unity and gifts, and the last verses on putting off the old self and putting on the new.
settingTheScene: Chapters 1 to 3 are doctrine; chapters 4 to 6 are practice. The word “therefore” at the start of chapter 4 connects them. The Christian life is a response to what God has done. Paul begins with the church’s unity, then moves to individuals: how to live as a new person. This chapter links with Psalm 68 and Psalm 110, which we read in the coming days.
observation: “I therefore, a prisoner for the Lord, urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling to which you have been called” (4:1).
“Eager to maintain the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace” (4:3).
“One Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all” (4:5-6).
“Rather, speaking the truth in love, we are to grow up in every way into him who is the head, into Christ” (4:15).
“To put on the new self, created after the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness” (4:24).
“Let no corrupting talk come out of your mouths, but only such as is good for building up” (4:29).
“And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption” (4:30).
“Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you” (4:32).
interpretation:
Paul, “a prisoner for the Lord,” urges the church to walk worthy of their calling: “with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, eager to maintain the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” Notice that unity is something we maintain, not create. The Spirit has already made us one. The basis is the seven “ones”: one body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all. The Trinity is the foundation of church unity.

Unity is not uniformity. “But grace was given to each one of us according to the measure of Christ’s gift.” Paul quotes Psalm 68:18: “When he ascended on high he led a host of captives, and he gave gifts to men.” The ascended Christ gives gifts to his church: apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds, and teachers, “to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up the body of Christ, until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to mature manhood, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ.” The goal is Christlikeness, and the means is the ministry of every member. Immaturity is marked by being “tossed to and fro by the waves and carried about by every wind of doctrine.” Maturity is marked by “speaking the truth in love” and growing into Christ.

Verses 17 to 24 describe the change. The Gentiles walk “in the futility of their minds,” darkened in understanding, hardened in heart, callous, given over to sensuality. “But that is not the way you learned Christ.” The imagery is clothing: put off the old self, which is corrupt through deceitful desires, be renewed in the spirit of your minds, and put on the new self, “created after the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness.” Holiness starts with a change of identity and shows up in daily choices.

Then practical commands, each with a reason. Put away falsehood and speak the truth, for we are members one of another. Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger. Let the thief no longer steal, but work, so that he may have something to share with the needy. Let no corrupting talk come out of your mouths, only what is good for building up. “And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.” The Spirit is a person who can be grieved by sin, especially by bitterness and malice. Instead: “Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you.” The standard of forgiveness is the cross.
connection: Psalm 68:18 is quoted in 4:8. Colossians 3:5-17 is a parallel on putting off and putting on. 1 Corinthians 12 and Romans 12 treat the gifts. John 17:20-23 is Jesus’ prayer for unity. Zechariah 8:16 stands behind 4:25. Psalm 4:4 is quoted in 4:26. Matthew 6:14-15 and 18:21-35 teach forgiveness. Hebrews 12:15 warns against a root of bitterness. 2 Corinthians 5:17 speaks of the new creation. 1 Thessalonians 5:19 says not to quench the Spirit.
application:
Identify one place where you could maintain unity: a strained relationship at church or home. Take a step.

Examine your words this week. Ask, is this good for building up?

Forgive someone as God in Christ forgave you, if you need to.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to help you walk worthy of your calling.
Ask him to make you humble, gentle, and patient.
Ask him to help you put off the old self and put on the new.
